headline: White-tailed eagles return to Exmoor after 200 years
summary: Six young eagles were released by Forestry England and the Roy Dennis Wildlife Foundation, with up to 20 more to come.
script: Six young white-tailed eagles have been released on Exmoor, two hundred years after the species vanished from the area. Conservationists plan up to twenty more over the next three years, restoring the coastline's native wildlife.
imageAlt: A young white-tailed eagle standing on a forest floor with dark and white feathers.
imageAltTwo: A white-tailed eagle in flight against a white sky.
